shared_fDTD_knowledge_used: 2.5x5.70 um body with 0.5 um guides centered at +/-0.4167 measured 3.41 dB/splitter, so narrow direct guides miss too much modal power.
The same body with 0.85 um mouths at +/-0.5336 measured 4.67 dB, so moving mouths outboard hurt despite widening.
The 2.5x5.5 um reference with 1.0 um mouths on about 10 um tapers centered +/-0.625 measured 1.08 dB, showing wide mouths that cover the inboard spots are the right direction.
reasoning: Tier-0 multimode physics gives a 3*Lpi/8 image length near 5.70 um for a 2.5 um SOI body, but the shared full-wave data shows the practical low-loss point is shorter, near 5.5 um, when wide tapered mouths collect the inboard images. I therefore used a 2.5 x 5.55 um MMI body, 1.0 um mouths, and moved the mouth centers slightly inboard from the 1.08 dB reference (+/-0.625 um) to +/-0.60 um, which is the minimum-gap-safe value for 1.0 um mouths. This preserves a 0.20 um mouth gap, covers the reported image spots near +/-0.42 um, and should reduce excess loss relative to the 1.08 dB reference without relying on a fake full-wave measurement. The MZI lower-arm meander was then lengthened laterally to restore the SOI FSR while keeping the original footprint.

predictions_not_measurements.predicted_basis: Interpolation from the measured 1.08 dB reference C, with the mouth centers moved slightly inboard while preserving 1.0 um mouth width and 0.20 um min gap.
predictions_not_measurements.predicted_extinction_ratio_db: >=20 if the conductor FDTD confirms near-50/50 splitting; the geometry is mirror-symmetric by construction.
